headline: Sells as too expensive at 17x EBIT with limited near-term catalyst unless M&A materialises
reasoning: Lynas trades on 17 times EBIT and only a 2.5% free cash flow yield, making it very expensive for a miner. The logical strategy for management would be to use expensive scrip to buy cheaper upstream assets. Laird would sell and look to get back in if M&A activity emerges.
quote: It's on 17 times EBIT or EBITR, which is super expensive for a miner. You know, trades on a two and a half percent free cash flow... I'll probably sell it to be honest.

headline: Luke Laird top pick Nickel Industries for 30-40% upside on 30% free cash flow yield into FY27 and vertically integrated low-cost model
reasoning: Nickel Industries' vertical integration in Indonesia means it benefits from rising nickel prices without the same margin compression that hits sulfide producers. Laird estimates a 30% free cash flow yield on the stock into FY27 with 30-40% price upside. The market is paying little attention to nickel names at present, creating a mispricing opportunity.
quote: We're actually estimating a 30 percent free cash flow yield on this stock into FY 27. So we don't think the market's sort of paying any attention to nickel mines at the moment... and see, you know, probably 30, 40 percent upside there.

headline: Luke Laird initiates buy on Pro-Medicus, seeing it as half the valuation of its peak with no peer on ASX for earnings quality
reasoning: Laird notes PME is now trading at roughly half its historical valuation or less. The business has $220 million cash, no debt, a buyback, and continues winning and renewing contracts. The quality, growth predictability and cashflow return on invested capital justifies a premium that few ASX companies can match. The executive departure does not undermine the IP-driven moat.
quote: Probably got to look at that in the context of, you know, cashflow return on invested capital and kind of the quality and growth and predictability of earnings growth here that you probably can't really get with almost any other company on the ASX. So, yeah, it'll be a buy for mine.

headline: Fair-valued with no clear outperformance catalyst versus alternatives like HCW
reasoning: Vicinity trades at fair value to its shopping centre assets and offers low-beta defensive exposure tied to interest rate cuts. As an active manager, Laird would rather deploy capital in higher-conviction ideas like HCW where there is a discernible catalyst and margin of safety.
quote: For vicinity, I wish I had a bit more to talk about here. In home states, the shopping center assets, it trades at fair value. I just don't see a huge opportunity for our performance here... I'd be a seller here.

headline: Luke Laird underweight Australian banks broadly, preferring ANZ and Westpac over NAB and CBA on relative valuation
reasoning: Australian banks are trading at 1.5 standard deviations above their average premium relative to global banking peers. Westpac at 16.5 times earnings and 1.7 times price to book is cheaper than CBA but still has further to fall toward long-run valuations of 12-14 times. If forced to own banks, Laird ranks ANZ and Westpac ahead of NAB and CBA.
quote: The Australian banks are broadly trading sort of at one and a half standard deviations above average premiums to relative major banking peers around the globe. So I think it's reasonable to be underweight Aussie banks at the moment.

headline: Luke Laird passes on Patronus Resources, preferring Matsu as cheaper alternative with larger resource and more exploration upside
reasoning: Patronus (a merger of Kin Mining and PNX Metals) looks cheap at 80 million market cap with 75 million in cash and investments, but cheap for a reason. Laird prefers Matsu (MAT), which has a larger resource of nearly one million ounces at 2.5g/t gold with exploration upside potentially reaching 600,000 to 2 million ounces at a cheaper price.
quote: I think from my perspective, Matsu's a better deal at a sort of cheaper price with maybe a bit more to do. So yeah, understanding appeal, but I think for me, MAT may be a better option.

headline: Luke Laird sells Orthocell as market cap well ahead of revenues at current growth stage with more downside likely
reasoning: Orthocell is growing revenues at 40-50% per annum and expanding into the US and Canada but is not yet profitable. With a market cap over $200 million against $3.2 million quarterly revenue, a lot of growth is already priced in. The stock is in the dangerous part of the micro-cap discovery curve where it can rerate quickly and has likely got ahead of itself.
quote: The market cap is kind of well over 200 million bucks now. So a fair bit of growth kind of baked in. And from our perspective, it's that sort of dangerous part of that micro cap kind of discovery curves... I'd be a seller here.

headline: Luke Laird sees value in near-production or takeover-candidate gold developers such as Canticle and Rox Minerals over expensive large producers
reasoning: Gold producers are expensive at current prices after two-to-three years of a significant bull market. Moving down the risk curve, near-production or likely takeover candidates like Canticle and Rox Minerals offer better value. For exploration exposure in tier-one jurisdictions, Laird prefers ALR (Alara Resources / ATR Minerals) in Guyana for exceptional value and exploration upside.
quote: Going down one level, you look at something like Cantipa or Rox Minerals, where you've got businesses that are almost in production or about to be taken over in our view.

headline: Luke Laird red hot buy on Healthco Healthcare and Wellness REIT at 60% discount to book with HealthScope resolution expected in 6-12 months as major catalyst
reasoning: HCW trades at a 60% discount to book value because its main tenant HealthScope is in administration, but HealthScope continues to pay rent in full and on time. Laird expects resolution within 6-12 months, which should trigger a dividend resumption and significant re-rating toward book value. HMC Capital has included HCW dividend resumption in its FY27 earnings guidance, confirming the expected timeline. Buying now offers a large margin of safety in quality assets with a time-constrained catalyst.
quote: This looks like a red hot buy to us. You're getting a huge discount to book valuation. You've got an upcoming catalyst for that valuation gap to close, as well as going to be, if you're buying at these prices, what we expect to be really strong dividends yield, which is currently not getting factored into the share price at all.

headline: Luke Laird avoids Centaurus Metals, preferring vertically integrated nickel assets over nickel sulfides competing against low-cost Indonesian supply
reasoning: Nickel sulfide projects have been rendered uneconomic by low-cost Chinese-backed Indonesian supply, as seen in BHP Nickel West, Mincor and IGO. Laird prefers vertically integrated nickel assets such as Nickel Industries (NIC) where vertical integration insulates against price compression and where he estimates a 30% free cash flow yield into FY27 with 30-40% upside.
quote: The nickel sulfides have just been completely competed out of the market due to kind of low cost Chinese back supply out of Indonesia. And that's just made everything in sulfides uneconomic.

headline: Luke Laird sees Megaport at fair value on 17x EV/EBITDA after recent spike, places on watch list for right price
reasoning: Laird previously made money on Megaport from $7 to $14 on inflecting profitability. After the recent 20% spike on Latitude acquisition performance, the stock sits at around 17 times EV/EBITDA, which he views as fair value. There is probably some upside but it may not clear risk-reward hurdles. The right price exists but the current level is not super enticing.
quote: I think on kind of 17 times EV to EBITDA, it's sort of fair value for this business, not super enticing for us here. Not that there's no upside. I think there probably is some that might not probably get over our hurdles on a risk-reward basis at the moment.

headline: Luke Laird recommends Matsu as better-value gold developer over Patronus, with nearly 1Moz resource and significant exploration upside
reasoning: Matsu has a large resource of almost one million ounces at 2.5 grams per tonne gold in Dunnora with exploration upside of 600,000 to potentially 2 million ounces. It offers better value than Patronus at a cheaper price with more resource growth potential.
quote: It's a bit cheaper. It's got a big resource in down and already of almost a million ounces of 2.5 grams per tonne gold and some sort of significant exploration upside. We think there's a target there of kind of 600 to maybe 2 million ounces.
